correctness.rationale: The statistic counts distinct nonempty palindrome strings of length at most one circuit, not occurrences or a length-by-length histogram. Partitioning by the number of ones is exhaustive. The zero- and one-marker counts are the largest gap and one plus the median gap, respectively. For two markers, each distinct internal gap gives a disjoint string family; its exterior radius is the maximum, among occurrences of that gap, of the minimum of its two neighbors. For three markers the two internal gaps must coincide and the two exterior zero strings share the unused gap, so their combined length is bounded by that gap. These arguments also work with zero gaps and with n=3. The resulting sums give all three stated formulas. With distinct gaps, n−3<=3γ−3, so γ>=ceil(n/3); solving for the smaller two gaps at equality gives the listed triples, and the difference from the repeated-gap count is positive for n>=14. Rotations and reversal generate all gap orderings of a multiset, yielding the claimed dihedral class counts. Fresh replay at branches/9e59a5c4-bfc7-46df-a136-31839cb7e520/independent_check.py enumerated actual palindrome strings for all 9,880 ordered gap triples through n=40 and reproduced the maximizing triples at every n=14,...,40. This is bounded evidence; the original uploaded verifier was not executed.

value.rationale: The three-marker slice is motivated by the known near-extremal circular family, not chosen as an arbitrary small instance. The complete count explains how coincidences between gaps change palindrome production and resolves exactly which three-marker circles attain or fall short of the restricted maximum. None of this is presented as an unrestricted binary-word extremum.
